key_insight: FlowLet introduces a wavelet-based flow matching generator to synthesize conditional high-resolution 3D brain MRIs (e.g., conditioned on age), allowing realistic, multi-scale MRI augmentation without collecting new scans.
problem_solved: Addresses demographic imbalance and scarcity in 3D brain MRI datasets for Brain Age Prediction by providing a method to generate diverse, age-conditional synthetic volumes to improve dataset balance and model generalization.
method: Wavelet multi-scale representation: decompose 3D MRIs into wavelet bands to model and synthesize coarse-to-fine anatomical structure efficiently.
Flow matching generative model: learn conditional continuous-time flows that map noise to realistic MRI volumes guided by age (or other covariates).
Conditional synthesis pipeline: combine wavelet reconstruction with flow-based sampling to produce high-fidelity 3D MRIs that preserve global anatomy and fine details.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical tool to augment and balance 3D MRI datasets for tasks like Brain Age Prediction, improving fairness and robustness without expensive or ethically constrained data collection. The multi-scale flow approach scales to high-resolution volumes while retaining anatomical realism.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: wavelet decomposition → conditional flow matching model → wavelet reconstruction (showing coarse-to-fine synthesis).
Side-by-side slices: real vs. synthetic 3D MRI slices across ages to demonstrate fidelity and age-conditioned variation.
Age-conditional interpolation: series of volumes or slice sequences showing smooth morphing across target ages.
Dataset balance chart: before/after augmentation bar chart showing improved age-distribution and class coverage.
paper_title: FlowLet: Conditional 3D Brain MRI Synthesis using Wavelet Flow Matching
paper_authors: Danilo Danese, Angela Lombardi, Matteo Attimonelli, Giuseppe Fasano, Tommaso Di Noia
